draft.title: British policy after 1763
card: Before 1763, Britain left the colonies to manage most of their own affairs. After 1763, it began to tighten its control.
Britain enforced laws on colonial trade more strictly, so colonists had less freedom over what they sold and where.
In 1763 the king banned settlement west of a line along the Appalachian Mountains. This limited where colonists could claim land.
Parliament passed new taxes on the colonies, such as the Stamp Act of 1765. They were set in London, not by colonial assemblies.
draft.remember: After 1763, Britain moved from loose oversight to firmer control through trade rules, a settlement limit and taxes.

a.q: Which change after 1763 best shows Britain tightening its control of the colonies?
opts: Britain limited where colonists could settle in the west
Britain let colonial assemblies set all trade rules
Britain removed all British officials from the colonies
Britain gave the colonies seats in the British parliament
a.why: Banning settlement west of a set line was a rule made in London that limited what colonists could do. The other options would give the colonies more freedom or a bigger say, not less.
a.clue: Which option takes a choice away from colonists?

b.q: Britain passed a new tax on printed items in the colonies in 1765. How does this fit British policy after 1763?
opts: It was one of several steps to tighten British control
It was a return to the loose control of earlier years
It was a reward for colonial help in the war with France
It was a law passed by colonial assemblies to fund defence
b.why: The tax was set by Britain and added to trade rules and the settlement limit as a sign of firmer control. It was not a reward or a colonial law, because colonial assemblies did not pass it.
b.clue: Who made this law, and did it give colonists more or less say?

a.best: Britain limited where colonists could settle in the west

b.best: It was one of several steps to tighten British control
